newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Euthanasia man's son backs move to overturn law.
newsitem.headline: Euthanasia man's son backs move to overturn law.

text.p: The son of the only person to die using the world's first euthanasia law in Australia's Northern Territory backed a campaign to overturn the law on Tuesday.
Rod Dent, the son of cancer patient Bob who used the law to die in September, was formerly a strong advocate of the right of terminally-ill patients to end their lives.
But Dent, a member of Australia's ruling Liberal party, said after a studying the Territory's law fully, he now believed it was unworkable and degraded the medical profession.
"No doctor in the Northern Territory is going to use this law, therefore, it makes the law invalid," Dent told reporters.

"What it does is denigrate the medical profession and the doctors down to the level of the gutter and I think once we get to the stage where the medical profession goes down to that level of society, we just end up in a giant abyss."
The Territory law allows terminally ill people who meet strict guidelines to kill themselves with a lethal injection or pills and for doctors to assist them to suicide.
In October, Australia's national parliament began debating government member Kevin Andrews' motion to overturn the law, which took effect in the Northern Territory in July.

The anti-euthanasia bill is still to face the non-government dominated upper house of parliament, the Senate, where its fate is uncertain. The national parliament has the power to overturn laws in Australia's two territories, but not the six states.
Dent called for the government to introduce a uniform law on best practice palliative care, saying he believed his father may not have ended his life if he had been adequately cared for.

"We need a national uniform law in regards to patients' rights under palliative care...to go right round Australia," Dent said. "I feel that had Bob Dent had access to the optimum palliative care in the Northern Territory, I believe he would have made a slightly different decision."
Dent rejected claims that the Liberal party had pressured him into changing his opinion on the law.
"I totally refute those allegations," he said.
"I've been under no pressure at all to make this decision."
The Northern Territory's law is also being challenged in Australia's High Court by a coalition of doctors, church and aboriginal leaders.
Euthanasia is illegal in the rest of Australia, but doctors say they unofficial assist terminally-ill patients to die.
